@graph.headline: Best Web3 PR Agencies in India in 2026
@graph.alternativeHeadline: The Indian media map, dual-track launch playbook, and how to choose between a local agency, a global agency, and a fractional APAC operator
@graph.description: A practical guide to Web3 PR in India in 2026: which outlets matter (Inc42, YourStory, Economic Times, Mint), how to run a dual-track launch across global crypto and India business press, what to look for in an Indian Web3 PR agency, and when a fractional senior APAC operator beats both. Includes the Bullieverse dual-track case and full pricing comparison.

itemListElement.name: Best Web3 PR Agencies in India in 2026

mainEntity.name: What is the best Web3 PR agency in India in 2026?

acceptedAnswer.text: There is no single best agency for every founder. The right answer depends on whether your primary need is India business press coverage (Inc42, YourStory, ET), global crypto press (CoinDesk, Cointelegraph), or both simultaneously. A full India-based Web3 agency typically runs INR-equivalent of $3K–$8K per month and has stronger local editorial depth. A global agency with India add-on runs $15K–$45K per month. A fractional senior APAC operator at $5K–$12K per month often delivers the dual-track capability that neither option handles alone. Ask any agency for named editorial placements, not wire pickups, in Inc42 or YourStory within the last 12 months before signing.

mainEntity.name: Which Indian media outlets matter most for a Web3 raise?

acceptedAnswer.text: For an India-based founder announcing a raise, the tier-1 targets are Inc42, YourStory, Economic Times, and Mint. Inc42 and YourStory are essential for reaching the Indian startup ecosystem and VC community. ET and Mint signal institutional legitimacy and reach a finance-professional and regulatory audience. Wire-only distribution without editorial India pickup will not build the home-market credibility that matters for future fundraising, hiring, and regulatory positioning.

mainEntity.name: How do you run a dual-track launch across global and India press?

acceptedAnswer.text: Offer the global crypto exclusive (CoinDesk, Cointelegraph, or Decrypt) three to five days before your announcement date, with an embargo to the launch date. Simultaneously offer a separate India-angle exclusive to Inc42 or YourStory with the same embargo date but a different narrative framing. Run wire distribution at embargo lift on the announcement day. Follow with India broadsheet pitches the next day using deeper data angles for the ET and Mint finance reader. The 72-hour window around the announcement day is where all of this must land. Managing the exclusives without breaking embargo with either editor is the operator skill that most founders underestimate.

mainEntity.name: What does India Web3 PR cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A full India-based Web3 agency typically runs INR-equivalent of $3,000–$8,000 per month. A global Web3 agency with India market coverage runs $15,000–$45,000 per month total. A fractional senior APAC operator with active India editorial relationships runs $5,000–$12,000 per month and is often the most cost-effective option for dual-track founders at pre-Series A or Series A. A launch sprint covering a single raise or mainnet event runs $15,000–$40,000 on a project basis.

mainEntity.name: Do Indian founders need separate PR for India and global markets?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not always separate agencies, but always separate narratives. The story that lands on CoinDesk is a protocol and technology story with global investor appeal. The story that lands on Inc42 is a founder-and-market story with India ecosystem context. Running one press release and hoping it works in both markets is the most common mistake Indian founders make. The dual-track launch means two distinct pitches, two distinct sets of editorial relationships, and two distinct timing tracks, managed so neither exclusive conflicts with the other.
